documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mr. Wright is 71, a retired letter carrier, transferring care after his longtime PCP retired. He wanted one doctor he can actually reach.

HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes for well over a decade, on basal insulin for years. Glargine 24 units at bedtime and aspart by a correction scale with meals; he checks sugars before meals and at bedtime. Reports morning sugars mostly 120s-160s. No lows he is aware of.
Hypertension on lisinopril and amlodipine for years.
Kidney function reduced for a few years; told stage 3. Never seen nephrology.
Coronary disease: one stent in 2022 at an outside hospital after chest pain. Follows with a cardiology group once a year. No chest pain or pressure since the stent. No orthopnea, no edema.
PAD is on his old list. He is not sure who found it. Denies leg pain with walking; walks around the neighborhood most days.
Cholesterol on atorvastatin 40 at night.

MEDICATIONS
Insulin glargine 24 units SC at bedtime
Insulin aspart SC with meals per correction scale
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Amlodipine 5 mg daily
Atorvastatin 40 mg at bedtime
Aspirin 81 mg daily

ALLERGIES: sulfa antibiotics (rash)

SURGICAL: coronary stent 2022.

FAMILY: father had an MI at 64. Mother had an ischemic stroke at 79. A sibling has type 2 diabetes and is on dialysis for kidney failure.

SOCIAL: Smoked for about forty years, 40 pack-years; quit in 2022 around the time of the stent. Does not drink. Retired from the postal service. Lives in Hadley.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, claudication, foot wounds, vision change, urinary symptoms.

EXAM
Well-appearing, conversational.
HEENT: anicteric. Neck: no JVD, no bruit.
Heart: regular, no murmur. Lungs: clear.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Ext: no edema. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses diminished but present bilaterally. Feet warm, skin intact, no calluses. Monofilament intact.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Type 2 diabetes on basal plus correction insulin. A1c today. Continue current doses for now.
2. CKD stage 3, likely diabetic and hypertensive. CMP and urine albumin/creatinine today.
3. Hypertension. In range today. Continue lisinopril and amlodipine.
4. CAD with stent 2022. Continue aspirin and atorvastatin. Keep annual cardiology.
5. PAD by history with diminished pulses. Will get an ABI so we have a baseline.
6. Former heavy smoker, quit 2022: eligible for annual low-dose CT; ordered. One-time aorta ultrasound for aneurysm screening ordered.
7. Lipids today.
8. Hep C screen today.
9. Records requested from prior practice.
Return in 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Mr. Wright,

Your labs are back. Your A1c is about where you guessed, a little under 8. Kidney function is in the same range your old office had on file, and potassium is fine on the lisinopril. Your LDL cholesterol is under 80 on the atorvastatin. The urine protein test is normal. Hepatitis C screen negative.

No medicine changes. I'll see you in December.

Your primary care physician

documents.title: Records from prior primary care practice
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Faxed records received from the patient's prior primary care office, 38 pages, scanned to chart.

Abstracted by front desk for the physician:
- Problem list on their last note: hypertension, type 2 diabetes on insulin, CKD stage 3, hyperlipidemia, coronary artery disease s/p PCI with stent 2022, peripheral arterial disease, tobacco use (quit 2022).
- Medication list matches what patient brought in.
- Allergy: sulfa (rash).
- Colonoscopy 2018: normal, no polyps. Repeat interval listed as 10 years.
- No cardiology catheterization report in the packet; stent noted by history only.
- Creatinine values on their flowsheet run 1.5 to 1.7 over the last two years.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:

Flu high-dose 0.7 mL IM left deltoid. PCV20 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. Lot numbers in the immunization record.
Tolerated well, waited 15 minutes, left in good spirits. Reminded about updated COVID shot at his pharmacy.

reports.text:
LIMITED ABDOMINAL AORTA ULTRASOUND, SCREENING
Indication: abdominal aortic aneurysm screening, male former smoker.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler imaging of the abdominal aorta from the diaphragm to the bifurcation, with the proximal common iliac arteries.
Findings: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber throughout, maximal outer-to-outer diameter 2.1 cm in the infrarenal segment. Proximal common iliac arteries are normal in caliber. No aneurysm. No periaortic fluid.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta. No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

documents.title: Ankle-Brachial Index
documents.author: vascular laboratory
documents.body:
ANKLE-BRACHIAL INDEX, RESTING
Indication: peripheral arterial disease by history; diminished pedal pulses.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics.
Technique: Doppler pressures at both brachial arteries and at the dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial arteries of each ankle, supine after 10 minutes of rest. Highest brachial pressure used as denominator.

Results:
Right ABI 0.84.
Left ABI 0.78.
Vessels were compressible.

Impression: Abnormal resting ABI on both sides, consistent with peripheral arterial disease, left lower than right.

reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (BASELINE)
Indication: 72-year-old former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2022.
Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest without contrast.
Findings: Lungs: no pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Heart normal in size. A coronary artery stent is noted. No pericardial effusion. Mediastinum: no adenopathy. Upper abdomen: unremarkable. Bones: no suspicious lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

Impression: stable coronary disease without angina.
Plan: continue current medicines. I will see him in a year, sooner if symptoms return.

Outside cardiology

documents.author: PCP

MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT

Health risk assessment reviewed with patient. Lives in Hadley, independent in all daily activities, drives, manages his own medicines and insulin. No falls in the past year. Hearing adequate for conversation. Vision corrected, eye exam November 2023 without retinopathy.
PHQ-2: 0.
Cognition: Mini-Cog 3-word recall 3/3, clock normal.
Advance directive: has a health care proxy form at home, not yet filed; asked him to bring a copy.

Problems reviewed: HTN, T2DM on insulin with CKD 3a, hyperlipidemia, CAD s/p stent 2022, PAD (ABI 0.84 R / 0.78 L), former smoker.
Medications reconciled, unchanged.
Allergy: sulfa antibiotics.

Prevention:
- Colonoscopy 2018 normal; next 2028 if still appropriate.
- LDCT October 2023 Lung-RADS 1; next due this fall.
- AAA screen done 2023, normal.
- Immunizations: flu and PCV20 fall 2023, COVID 2023-24, Shingrix complete. RSV recommended this fall given diabetes and CKD.
- Hep C negative 2023.

Exam: well, BMI per vitals. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet without lesions; pulses diminished bilaterally.

Plan: annual labs today. Diabetes follow-up in September. RSV and flu in the fall.

documents.title: Was in the hospital
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I was in the hospital from last Friday till Tuesday. Had chest pressure Friday morning sitting at the kitchen table that would not quit so I called 911. They kept me and did a heart cath Monday through the left groin. They said no new stent was needed and to keep taking the same pills. They said I should see you and my heart doctor. I feel ok now. Groin is a little sore. Do you want to see me? Roger

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thank you for letting me know, Roger. Glad you are feeling better. Yes, I'd like to see you next week; the front desk will call with a time. We'll request the hospital records. If the chest pressure comes back, call 911 again, don't wait for us. If the groin gets more swollen, very bruised or painful, call the same day.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Patient: Roger Wright, 72M. Arrival 10/20/2024 13:25.

CC: Left foot pain x2 days.

HPI: 72-year-old man with diabetes on insulin, hypertension, CKD, hyperlipidemia, coronary disease with prior stent and peripheral arterial disease, who had a diagnostic heart catheterization for unstable angina three weeks ago. Two days of severe, sharp, constant pain in the left foot that gets worse when he props the leg up. Over the past couple of weeks he has also had brief spells of disturbed vision that clear on their own, and belly pain that comes on after meals.

HOME MEDS: insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin aspart correction scale with meals, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.
ALLERGIES: sulfa antibiotics (rash).
FH: father MI at 64, mother ischemic stroke at 79, sibling with type 2 diabetes and kidney failure on dialysis.
SH: ex-smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2022. No alcohol. Retired from the post office.

EXAM: Left foot cool compared with the right, one toe cyanotic. Lacy, net-like mottling over both lower legs. Fundoscopy: bright refractile plaques where retinal arterioles branch. Groin access site healed.

DATA: creatinine 2.8 mg/dL (his baseline 1.6), BUN 44, CBC within normal limits, CRP 46 mg/L, ESR 58 mm/h.

MDM: Blue toe, livedo, retinal cholesterol plaques and a sharp creatinine rise three weeks after a catheter procedure: cholesterol embolization syndrome with acute kidney injury. Admit to medicine for renal monitoring and pain control.

DISPOSITION: admitted.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/20/2024. Discharged 10/23/2024.

Principal diagnosis: atheroembolism (cholesterol embolism syndrome) following coronary angiography 9/30/2024.
Secondary: acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3; type 2 diabetes on insulin; hypertension; coronary artery disease; peripheral arterial disease.

Hospital course: Presented with left foot pain, a cyanotic toe, livedo of the lower legs and retinal cholesterol plaques three weeks after femoral catheterization. Creatinine 2.8 on arrival from a baseline of 1.6. Managed supportively with fluids as tolerated, foot care and pain control. Aspirin and atorvastatin continued. No anticoagulation was given. Creatinine 2.5 on the morning of discharge. Foot pain improved; toe remained dusky but viable.

Discharge medications (no changes): insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin aspart correction scale, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics.

Follow-up: primary care within one week with a basic metabolic panel. Cardiology as scheduled.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Patient called: discharged today from a second hospital stay since Sunday 10/20 for left foot pain and a blue toe. He says they told him small pieces of cholesterol broke loose after the heart cath and his kidneys took a hit. No discharge papers sent to us yet. Same medicines. Foot pain better than Sunday, toe still a bit purple. Eating and drinking ok, urinating normally. No chest pain.
Scheduled Monday 10/28 with PCP, bloodwork same day. Advised to keep the foot protected, no heating pad, and call or go to the ED for a black or open toe, fever, or much less urine.

events.reason: follow-up after hospitalization, atheroembolism and kidney injury

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Admission 10/20-10/23/2024. ED record received 10/25 and reviewed; discharge summary not yet received.

Summary from the ED record and patient: three weeks after the 9/30 diagnostic coronary angiography through the left femoral artery, he developed severe left foot pain, a cyanotic toe, livedo of both lower legs, retinal cholesterol plaques on fundoscopy, brief visual disturbances and post-meal belly pain. Creatinine 2.8 from baseline 1.6, BUN 44, CRP and ESR elevated, CBC normal. Diagnosed with cholesterol embolization and acute kidney injury. Told no medicine changes.

Today: foot pain much less, takes nothing for it now. Toe still dusky. Vision has been normal since the hospital. Belly pain after meals has settled. Urinating normally. Sugars a little higher in the hospital, back to his usual at home.

Exam: afebrile. Comfortable. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Legs: faint lacy mottling persists over both shins. One toe on the left foot dusky violaceous, cool at the tip, capillary refill slow, skin intact, no ulceration or black areas. Left foot otherwise warm. Pedal pulses diminished as before.

Creatinine today 2.3, coming down.

A/P
1. Atheroembolism (cholesterol embolism syndrome) after femoral catheterization, with acute kidney injury on CKD 3a. Supportive care. Continue aspirin and atorvastatin. Avoid any new vascular procedures if possible. Protect the foot. Recheck BMP in 3 weeks.
2. Unstable angina 9/2024 managed medically. Cardiology in December.
3. T2DM: same insulin.
4. Medication reconciliation done; list unchanged.
Call for any skin breakdown on the toe.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis without contrast
reports.text:
CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST
Indication: severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, vomiting, elevated lipase. IV contrast withheld for reduced kidney function.
Findings: Peripancreatic inflammatory stranding and edema surrounding the pancreas. No organized peripancreatic collection. Liver, spleen and adrenal glands unremarkable. Gallbladder unremarkable without dense stones. No biliary dilation. Kidneys without hydronephrosis. Bowel loops are not obstructed. Abdominal aorta normal in caliber. No free air.
reports.conclusion: Findings of acute pancreatitis: peripancreatic inflammation and edema.

reports.text:
RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ULTRASOUND
Indication: acute pancreatitis, evaluate for gallstones.
Findings: Gallbladder normally distended, no stones, no sludge, no wall thickening, no pericholecystic fluid; sonographic Murphy sign negative. Common bile duct 4 mm, not dilated. No intrahepatic ductal dilation. Liver normal in echotexture. Pancreas partially obscured by bowel gas.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admission 4/25/2025, discharge 4/29/2025.

Principal diagnosis: acute pancreatitis.
Secondary: acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease stage 3; type 2 diabetes on insulin; hypertension; coronary artery disease; peripheral arterial disease; history of cholesterol embolization (10/2024).

Presentation: about six hours of severe, steady upper abdominal pain boring through to the back, with nausea and repeated vomiting. Denied chest pain, shortness of breath and any change in bowel habits. In the ED: BP 165/90, HR 102, temperature 38.2 C. Abdomen distended and tender in the epigastrium with hypoactive bowel sounds.
ED labs: WBC 16.0, hemoglobin 13.2, BUN 31, creatinine 2.1 (baseline 1.6), glucose 210, amylase 900 U/L, lipase 1100 U/L.
CT abdomen/pelvis without contrast: inflammation and edema around the pancreas.

Hospital course: Treated with IV fluids, bowel rest and IV analgesia. Right upper quadrant ultrasound showed no gallstones and no duct dilation. Triglycerides 172. He does not drink alcohol. No cause was established. Pain settled by day 3 and diet was advanced, tolerated. Insulin continued with dose adjustment while not eating, then home doses resumed. Creatinine 1.9 at discharge.

Discharge medications (unchanged from admission): insulin glargine 24 units at bedtime, insulin aspart correction scale, lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (rash).

Follow-up: primary care in 1 week with BMP.

documents.title: Hospital again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hello, I was in the hospital again last Friday to Tuesday. Pancreatitis they said. Terrible pain in my stomach going to my back and throwing up. They did a CT and an ultrasound, no gallstones. I'm eating soft stuff now and feel much better. They said to see you in a week and get bloodwork. Can I get in Monday or Tuesday? Roger

documents.title: RE: Hospital again
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Hi Mr. Wright, we have you Monday 5/5 at 1:20 with your doctor, labs at the visit. Please bring any discharge papers you were given. We have requested the hospital records.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Admitted 4/25-4/29/2025 with acute pancreatitis. No hospital records yet; he brought his discharge instruction sheet, which lists the diagnosis, no medicine changes, and a BMP in a week. Records requested today.

He describes six hours of severe upper belly pain going into the back with vomiting before he went in. CT and gallbladder ultrasound done; he was told no gallstones and that they did not find a cause. He does not drink.
Now: eating regular meals since Saturday without pain. No nausea. Bowels normal. No fever. Sugars back to his usual range at home; glargine 24 and scale aspart as before. No chest pain. Feet fine.

Exam: afebrile, looks well. Abdomen soft, nondistended, no tenderness, normal bowel sounds. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema.

A/P
1. Acute pancreatitis, recovering; cause not identified on the hospital's workup per patient. Lipase, CBC today. Diet as tolerated.
2. AKI with the pancreatitis: BMP today.
3. T2DM, HTN, CAD/PAD, prior atheroembolism: no changes.
Will review the summary when it comes. Wellness visit in June.

documents.title: Lab result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Lipase normal. White count normal. Creatinine 1.9, better than the 2.1 he had in the ED but higher than his January 1.6. Recheck at the June visit to see where it settles.

documents.title: Records received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Discharge summary for the April 2025 admission received by fax today, filed under that admission and routed to PCP. ED physician record was not included; the hospital says the summary is what they release for this request.

documents.title: Outside summary reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Lipase 1100, amylase 900, WBC 16.0, creatinine 2.1 on arrival; CT with peripancreatic edema, RUQ US without stones, TG 172. No cause named. Matches what he told us. Nothing new to act on.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE ANNUAL WELLNESS VISIT

Interval: hard year. Unstable angina with diagnostic cath 9/2024 (records still not received), cholesterol emboli with AKI 10/2024, acute pancreatitis 4/2025. Feels back to himself now. Eating normally, no abdominal pain since discharge. No chest pain. Walking most days.

HRA: independent in ADLs and IADLs, drives, does his own insulin. No falls. Hearing fine. Eyes checked January, no retinopathy.
PHQ-2: 0. Mini-Cog 3/3, normal clock.
Health care proxy copy now in the chart.

Medications reconciled; unchanged.
Allergy: sulfa antibiotics.

Exam: well. Heart regular, lungs clear, abdomen soft and nontender. Feet: skin intact, pulses diminished as before, monofilament intact.

Kidney function: creatinine 1.9 today, same as May, now the third value at that level since April. eGFR in the high 30s. Restaging CKD to 3b. This is his new baseline after two kidney injuries.

A/P
- Acute pancreatitis: resolved.
- AKI: resolved, new baseline as above.
- CKD 3b: continue lisinopril, BP control; avoid NSAIDs (he doesn't use them). Annual urine albumin today.
- T2DM: A1c today.
- Lipids today on atorvastatin 40.
- Prevention: Tdap today. LDCT due December. Flu, COVID in the fall. Colonoscopy 2028 if appropriate.
Follow-up September.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Quiet summer, no ED trips. Sugars fasting 120-160 on glargine 24 and the aspart scale. No readings below 70 in the meter memory we looked at together. No abdominal pain. No chest pain, no leg pain with walking.
O: vitals reviewed. Heart RRR, lungs clear, abdomen benign, feet intact with diminished pulses.
A/P:
- T2DM with CKD 3b: A1c and BMP today; no change.
- HTN: continue.
- CAD/PAD/history of atheroembolism: aspirin, atorvastatin.
- Flu and COVID vaccines next month; nurse visit booked.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 10/26/2025 (ICU 10/26-10/28, then medical floor). Discharged 10/31/2025.

Principal diagnosis: severe hypoglycemia with altered mental status.
Secondary: sepsis from a urinary source, Escherichia coli; acute kidney injury on CKD stage 3b; type 2 diabetes on insulin; hypertension; coronary artery disease; peripheral arterial disease; history of atheroembolism and of acute pancreatitis.

Presentation: brought in by ambulance from home, confused and drowsy. On arrival lethargic but rousable, skin warm and dry. BP 95/60, HR 102, RR 22, temperature 38.3 C. Glucose 48. Creatinine 2.8 (baseline 1.9), BUN 44, potassium 4.5, sodium 135. Arterial gas: pH 7.32, PaCO2 32, HCO3 18.

Course: IV dextrose with recovery of mental status; glucose monitored hourly in the ICU. IV fluids and IV ceftriaxone for urosepsis. Urine culture grew E. coli susceptible to ceftriaxone; blood cultures no growth. Insulin held at first, then basal resumed at a lower dose: glargine 18 units at bedtime, aspart correction scale with meals. No further hypoglycemia on the floor. Creatinine 2.3 on the day of discharge.

Discharge medications:
- insulin glargine 18 units SC at bedtime (DECREASED from 24)
- insulin aspart correction scale with meals (unchanged)
- cefpodoxime 200 mg by mouth twice daily to complete 10 days of antibiotic therapy (NEW)
- lisinopril 10 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, aspirin 81 mg daily (unchanged)
Allergies: sulfonamide antibiotics (rash).

Follow-up: primary care within one week; BMP.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily to complete 10 days of antibiotics

documents.title: Pharmacy call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Saturday call from patient's pharmacy. They filled cefpodoxime 200 mg BID yesterday and a new glargine prescription for 18 units at bedtime from a hospital discharge, and wanted to confirm which glargine dose is current since our refill on file says 24 units. We had no notice of a hospitalization.
Called patient: admitted 10/26 to 10/31, found confused at home with a low sugar and a urine infection, in the ICU two days. Feels weak but ok. Taking the antibiotic. Has been taking 18 units since discharge; sugars 140s-180s, no lows.
Told pharmacy to follow the 18-unit discharge prescription. Our list still shows 24 units; PCP to reconcile. Post-hospital visit booked Tuesday 11/4. Advised patient to check sugars 4 times a day and call for anything under 70.

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TRANSITIONAL CARE VISIT
Admission 10/26-10/31/2025. We learned of it from the pharmacy on 11/1. No discharge summary yet; patient brought his discharge medication list.

Per patient and his paperwork: found confused at home early Sunday and taken by ambulance. Sugar was very low and he had a fever; urine infection that got into his blood. ICU for two days. Glargine cut from 24 to 18 units. Antibiotic, cefpodoxime, through Wednesday. He does not remember the morning he was brought in. He had not changed his insulin doses before it happened.

Now: no fever, no urinary complaints. Energy coming back. Sugars since discharge: fasting 140-190, pre-supper 150-200, no lows. Uses aspart only for readings over 200.

Exam: afebrile, alert, oriented. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft; no CVA tenderness. Feet intact, pulses diminished as before.
Creatinine today 2.1.

A/P
1. Severe hypoglycemia with altered mental status during E. coli urosepsis and AKI on CKD 3b, on basal insulin. Updated our list to glargine 18 units at bedtime; stopped the 24-unit order. Glucagon nasal powder prescribed; reviewed when and how to use it. A1c goal relaxed to under 8 given the low and his kidneys. Check sugars at least twice a day plus any time he feels off.
2. Urosepsis, E. coli: finishing cefpodoxime. Feels well.
3. AKI on CKD 3b: creatinine improving. BMP in about 5 weeks.
4. HTN, CAD/PAD: unchanged.
Will review the summary when it arrives. Follow-up in December.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine back to 1.9, his baseline since spring. Kidney injury resolved. Hospital summary received 11/7 and reviewed: urine culture E. coli, blood cultures negative, glargine reduced to 18. Infection treated; no lows reported since. Closing out the acute problems. Message to patient.

documents.title: Kidney test
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Roger, your kidney numbers are back to where they were before the hospital stay. Keep the glargine at 18 units and keep the glucagon handy. See you in February.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING (ANNUAL)
Indication: former smoker, 40 pack-years, quit 2022.
Comparison: 12/19/2024 and 10/26/2023.
Technique: low-dose helical CT of the chest, no IV contrast.
Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Lungs clear without consolidation. No pleural effusion. Heart normal size; coronary stent. No adenopathy. Upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1. Negative screen; next annual screen in 12 months.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First visit since the October hospital stay settled down. Glargine 18 at bedtime, aspart only for readings over 200, a few times a week. Fasting 140s to 170s. Lowest reading in the meter since November is 92. Glucagon at home, unused; he keeps it next to his meter. No urinary symptoms. No chest pain, no leg pain with walking.
Saw cardiology in December for the yearly visit; he says they listened, did an ECG, and changed nothing. We never got a letter.

O: vitals as charted. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. Feet: skin intact, pulses diminished as before.

A/P
- T2DM with CKD 3b, recent severe hypoglycemia: A1c today, goal under 8. Keep glargine 18.
- CKD 3b: BMP today.
- HTN: continue lisinopril 10, amlodipine 5.
- CAD/PAD, history of atheroembolism: aspirin, atorvastatin 40. Requesting the December cardiology note.
RTC 3 months. Records request, cardiology visit 12/2025.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from 4/15. Doing well. Sugars fasting 130-170, no lows, glucagon still unused. No hospital visits. No abdominal pain, no chest pain, no foot problems.
Exam: regular rhythm, clear lungs, no edema, feet intact.
February A1c was 8.3, a little above the under-8 goal; after last fall's low he would rather run slightly high, and so would I.
Plan: A1c and BMP today; no insulin change. The cardiology letter from December still has not come. Wellness visit in June.
